abstract: The arms race between bacteria and bacteriophages (phages) gave rise to multiple layers of antagonistic mechanisms, many of which remain unexplored. Here, we investigated the widespread anti-phage defense system GAPS4. We found that GAPS4 forms a heterotetrameric complex containing active PD-(D/E)xK phosphodiesterase domains. It is triggered upon sensing DNA damage, leading to genomic DNA degradation and cell suicide. We further demonstrated that this activation mechanism renders GAPS4 a double-edged sword, sensitizing bacteria to various DNA-targeting antibacterial agents. Collectively, our findings reveal a possible evolutionary trade-off between anti-phage defense and immunity against interbacterial antagonism.
